wizard_welcome_intro: CC Mosquitto is a message broker for your IoT sensors and ChromaChecker Capture stations. It acts as a central hub — sensors send temperature, humidity, and other data here, and your Capture applications pick it up automatically.
wizard_welcome_hint: This wizard appears on first launch. You can run it again from Help → Setup Wizard.
wizard_network_explain: These settings control how devices find and connect to your broker. In most cases the defaults work perfectly.
wizard_network_port_help: The standard MQTT port is 1883. Change it only if another service already uses this port. Every device (sensors, Capture stations) must use the same port number.
wizard_security_explain: A username and password prevent unauthorized devices from connecting to your broker. This is recommended — without it, anyone on your network can read your sensor data.
wizard_security_where_title: Where do I enter this password later?
wizard_security_where_text: You will need to enter the same username and password in three places:
wizard_security_where_1: Here — CC Mosquitto (you're doing this now)
wizard_security_where_2: ChromaChecker Capture — on each computer running Capture, go to Device → MQTT Broker → Setup and enter the same credentials
wizard_security_where_3: Each sensor — in the sensor's web interface (Shelly: Settings → MQTT; Tasmota: Configuration → MQTT), enter the same credentials
wizard_security_where_note: All three must match. If any device has the wrong password, it won't be able to connect.
wizard_ready_autostart: Start broker automatically when I log in
wizard_ready_next_1: Click Finish to save your settings and start the broker
wizard_ready_next_2: On each ChromaChecker Capture computer, open Device → MQTT Broker → Setup and enter the broker address and credentials
wizard_ready_next_3: Configure your sensors to connect to this broker (see the Network Guide tab for detailed instructions)
wizard_ready_next_4: Watch the Connection Log tab — you should see devices connecting
